abstract: This paper studies what happens when AI gets cheaper, with emphasis on the labor market outcomes, whether it creates formal jobs or whether it pushes workers into informality. We argue that the answer depends on the elasticity of substitution between imported AI capital and formal labor. We build a small open economy DSGE model with a dual labor market, imported AI capital, and country risk, calibrated to an economy where informality is pervasive. The same decline in AI prices produces sharply different labor-market outcomes depending on whether AI substitutes or complements formal workers. Under substitution, cheaper AI weakens formal labor demand and increases the role of the informal sector as an employment buffer. Under complementarity, it expands formal employment and amplifies output, wages, investment, and capital accumulation. The model therefore shows that AI can become either a source of displacement pressure or a driver of formal-sector expansion, depending on how it interacts with human labor.

ob.ai_reason: 核心是AI对劳动力市场影响，劳动经济学
ob.tldr: 构建小型开放经济DSGE模型，纳入正规与非正规双重劳动力市场及进口AI资本，分析AI降价对发展中经济体的劳动力影响。结果取决于AI与正规劳动的替代弹性：替代关系下正规就业收缩、非正规部门扩大充当缓冲；互补关系下则扩张正规就业、放大产出和工资。AI既可能成为劳动力替代压力，也可能成为正规部门扩张驱动力，取决于其与人力劳动的交互方式。

title: Cheaper AI, More Informality? A Dual Labor Market Model for Developing Economies
title_zh: 更便宜的AI，更多的非正规性？面向发展中经济体的二元劳动力市场模型
